subject: Is the horse shoe / hierarchical shrinkage prior considered an improper prior?

messages.author: a0f5c47e0d2e4773
messages.subject: Is the horse shoe / hierarchical shrinkage prior considered an improper prior?
parts: I've been trying to compute point null hypotheses with the hypothesis function, but alas, NA is returned for any point hypothesis test. I know that you have to have a proper prior on all parameters, which I have on the other parameters in the model, so I don't think any of the other priors would be the issue.

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Is the horse shoe / hierarchical shrinkage prior considered an improper prior?
parts: the horseshoe prior is proper but is parameterized in a certain (efficient and stable) way in brms that cannot be captured by the function that allows to sample from priors. accordingly you currently cannot test point hypothesis using this approach, but you can use the bayes_factor function to compare the two models (one with and one without the restriction).
